topic: What if all the bees disappeared? About one third of the food crops we eat depend on pollinators like bees.

episode.title: What If All the Bees Disappeared?

shots.narration: What if all the bees disappeared?
shots.scene: Colourful 3D science lab, vertical 9:16 frame, glowing garden hologram between Nova and Byte, no text or symbols.
shots.action: Nova sweeps the holographic bees out of the garden.
shots.mood: Bright turquoise lighting, curious expressions, suddenly empty flowers.

shots.narration: Bees carry pollen between flowers, helping many plants make seeds.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a large flower hologram at Byte's eye level, vertical composition, no text.
shots.action: A holographic bee transfers golden pollen between two flowers.
shots.mood: Warm pink petals, sparkling pollen, fascinated faces.

shots.narration: [surprised] About one third of our food crops depend on pollinators.
shots.scene: Lab hologram showing crop models arranged in three equal clusters, one cluster glowing gold, no labels or numbers.
shots.action: Nova points to the glowing cluster of pollinator-dependent crops.
shots.mood: Colourful produce, golden illumination, wide-eyed discovery.

shots.narration: Butterflies, flies, and other animals also pollinate flowers.
shots.scene: Vertical lab garden hologram with oversized blossoms and tiny holographic butterflies and flies, no text.
shots.action: Byte magnifies the other pollinators visiting blossoms.
shots.mood: Lively green foliage, delicate wings, reassuring blue glow.

shots.narration: Without bees, many crops would produce fewer fruits and seeds.
shots.scene: Lab hologram containing adjacent apple branches, one heavily fruited and one sparsely fruited, no labels.
shots.action: Nova reveals the sparsely fruited branch inside the hologram.
shots.mood: Clear visual contrast, thoughtful expressions, gentle amber lighting.

shots.narration: [sighs] Our meals could become less varied, with fewer bee-dependent foods.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a holographic meal containing apples, almonds, bread and rice, no text.
shots.action: Byte reduces the apple and almond portions on the holographic plate.
shots.mood: Noticeable empty plate space, concerned screen eyes, soft lighting.

shots.narration: But rice and wheat don't need bees for pollination.
shots.scene: Bright lab with a tall hologram of golden wheat and green rice plants, no labels.
shots.action: Nova enlarges the wheat and rice hologram.
shots.mood: Golden light, sturdy grain heads, relieved smiles.

shots.narration: Protecting wild habitats helps bees and other pollinators thrive.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a holographic meadow surrounding farmland, native flowers and nesting patches, no text.
shots.action: Nova expands the flowering habitat around the holographic fields.
shots.mood: Lush greens, abundant blossoms, hopeful purple and blue lighting.

shots.narration: [excited] Wind pollinates wheat—what if Earth lost its wind?
shots.scene: Vertical lab hologram of wheat beneath a floating Earth, visible golden pollen and translucent airflow ribbons, no text.
shots.action: A holographic breeze carries pollen between wheat flower heads.
shots.mood: Glowing golden particles, swirling blue ribbons, delighted curiosity.

episode.endHook: Wheat relies on wind—but what if Earth lost its wind?
episode.description: Dr. Nova shows Byte how disappearing bees would change our food supply. Explore pollination, the foods we'd miss, and the surprising crops that don't need bees.
